chanterelle.label: Chanterelle (Cantharellus)
chanterelle.note: Mycorrhizal with oak. Fruits 1-3 weeks after a soak and persists; wants sustained moisture rather than one downpour.

black_trumpet.label: Black trumpet (Craterellus)
black_trumpet.note: Mycorrhizal with oak, usually in mossy, low, damp ground nearby. Wants sustained moisture even more than chanterelles and hides well in leaf litter -- look, don't just glance.

bolete.label: Boletes (edible Boletus spp.)
bolete.note: Mycorrhizal with both oak and pine, so pine barrens count. Flushes hard 5-14 days after rain and passes quickly.

chicken.label: Chicken-of-the-woods (Laetiporus)
chicken.note: Decays oak wood, living or dead, so scattered big trees count and it is the least soil-moisture dependent of the five.

hen.label: Hen-of-the-woods (Grifola frondosa)
hen.note: At the base of large, mature, often stressed oaks. Tight autumn window, triggered by the first run of cool nights (nights in the 50s F) -- the season term below waits for them.
hen.season_phase: waiting for cooler nights (7-day mean low 14 C, full credit at 13 C)
